exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Value of the Remainder When a Polynomial is Divided by a Linear Factor

question.text: The remainder of dividing $2x^4 + x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x - 7$ by $x +1$ is
question.explanation:
Let $p(x) = 2x^4 + x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x - 7.$

The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x+1),$ the remainder equals $p(-1).$

Evaluating $p(-1)$ directly gives \begin{align} p(-1) & = 2(-1)^4 + (-1)^3 - 2(-1)^2 - 3(-1) - 7\\[3pt] & = 2 - 1 - 2 + 3 - 7\\[3pt] & = -5. \end{align}

So, when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x+1),$ the remainder is $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-5}.$

Note: We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

$x^4$ $x^3$ $x^2$ $x^1$ $x^0$
$\color{red}-1$ $2$ $1$ $-2$ $-3$ $-7$
$\color{gray}\downarrow$ $-2$ $1$ $1$ $2$
$2$ $-1$ $-1$ $-2$ $-5$

question.text: Find the remainder of the division $\dfrac{-3x^4 + 7x^3 - 4x^2 - x + 7}{x - 2}.$
question.explanation:
Let $p(x) = -3x^4 + 7x^3 - 4x^2 - x + 7.$

The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-2),$ the remainder equals $p(2).$

Evaluating $p(2)$ directly gives \begin{align} p(2) & = -3(2)^4 + 7(2)^3 - 4(2)^2 - 2 + 7\\[3pt] & = -48 + 56 - 16 - 2 + 7\\[3pt] & = -3. \end{align}

So, when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-2),$ the remainder is $-3.$

Note: We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

$x^4$ $x^3$ $x^2$ $x^1$ $x^0$
$\color{red}2$ $-3$ $7$ $-4$ $-1$ $7$
$\color{gray}\downarrow$ $-6$ $2$ $-4$ $-10$
$-3$ $1$ $-2$ $-5$ $-3$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Value of a Single Unknown in a Polynomial Given a Remainder

question.text: Find the value of $k$ if the remainder of the division $\dfrac{x^3+kx+1}{x+1}$ is $0.$
question.explanation:
Let $q(x)=x^3+kx+1.$

The remainder theorem states that when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x+1),$ the remainder equals $q(-1).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $0,$ then, we must have $q(-1)=0.$

Evaluating $q(-1)$ directly gives \begin{align*} q(-1) &= (-1)^3+k(-1)+1\\ &= -1-k+1\\ &=- k, \end{align*}

which means that $k=0.$

question.text: When $ x^3+7x^2+x+a$ is divided by $x+7$ the remainder is $2.$ What is the value of $a?$
question.explanation:
The remainder theorem states that when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x+7),$ the remainder equals $q(-7).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $2,$ then we must have $q(-7)=2.$

Evaluating $q(-7)$ directly gives \begin{align*} q(-7) &= (-7)^3 +7(-7)^2+(-7)+a \\[5pt] &= -343 + 343 -7 + a\\[5pt] &= -7+a, \end{align*} which means that \[ 2 = -7+a. \]

Solving for $a$ in the equation above, we find that $a = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{9}.$

question.text: If the remainder of the division $\dfrac{x^4 - px^3+2x^2+5x+7}{x+2}$ is $q,$ express $p$ in terms of $q.$
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=x^4 - px^3+2x^2+5x+7.$

The remainder theorem states that when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+2),$ the remainder equals $f(-2).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $q,$ then, we must have $f(-2)=q.$

Evaluating $f(-2)$ directly gives \begin{align*} f(-2) &= (-2)^4-p(-2)^3+2(-2)^2+5(-2)+7\\[5pt] &=16+8p+8-10+7\\[5pt] &= 21+8p, \end{align*}

which means that

\[ q =21+8p. \]

Solving for $p$ in the equation above, we find that $p = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{q-21}{8}}.$

question.text: When $p(x) = 9x^3 + mx^2 + x - 2$ is divided by $3x - 1$ the remainder is $2.$ What is the value of $m?$
question.explanation:
The remainder theorem states that when $p(x)$ is divided by $3x - 1 = 3\left(x - \dfrac{1}{3}\right),$ the remainder equals $p\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right).$ Since we're told that the remainder is $2,$ then, we must have $p\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 2.$

Evaluating $p\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$ directly gives \begin{align*} p\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) & = 9\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3 + m\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{3} - 2\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{m}{9} + \dfrac{1}{3} - 2 \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{m}{9} - \dfrac{4}{3}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{m - 12}{9}, \end{align*} which means that \[ 2 = \dfrac{m - 12}{9}. \]

Solving for $m$ in the equation above, we find that $m = 30.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Values of Two Unknowns in a Polynomial Given Two Remainders

question.text: Suppose $f(x)=ax^2+bx-6$ has a factor of $(x-3)$ and has a remainder of $-4$ when divided by $(x+1).$ Find the value of $a+b.$
question.explanation:
Since $(x-3)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, it must divide into $f(x)$ with no remainder. In other words, when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x-3),$ the remainder is $0.$ It follows from the remainder theorem that

\begin{align*} 0 &= f(3)\\ &= a(3)^2 + b(3) - 6\\ &= a(9) + b(3) - 6\\ &= 9a + 3b - 6. \end{align*}

Likewise, since we're told that the remainder is $-4$ when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+1),$ it follows from the remainder theorem that \begin{align*} -4 &= f(-1)\\ &= a(-1)^2 + b(-1) - 6\\ &= a(1) + b(-1) - 6\\ &= a - b - 6. \end{align*}

We now have the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} 0 = 9a + 3b - 6 \\ -4 = a -b - 6. \end{cases} \]

Simplifying each equation, we get

\[ \begin{cases} 3a + b = 2 \\ a - b = 2. \end{cases} \]

To eliminate $b,$ we add the equations and get

\[ \begin{alignat}{2} 3&a+b &&= 2 \\ + \hspace{7pt} &a-b &&= 2 \\ \hline 4&a &&= 4. \end{alignat} \]

So, we get $a=1.$ Finally, we substitute it into $a - b = 2$ to find $b=-1.$

Therefore, our final solution is $(a,b) = (1,-1).$

Finally then, $a+b=1-1=0.$

example.title: Finding the Values of Two Unknowns in a Polynomial Given Two Remainders

question.text: Suppose $f(x)=ax^2+bx-10$ has a factor of $x+2$ and has a remainder of $18$ when divided by $x+4.$ Find the value of $a+b.$
question.explanation:
Since $(x+2)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, it must divide into $f(x)$ with no remainder. In other words, when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+2),$ the remainder is $0.$ It follows from the remainder theorem that

\begin{align*} 0 &= f(-2)\\ &= a(-2)^2 + b(-2) - 10\\ &= a(4) + b(-2) - 10\\ &= 4a - 2b - 10. \end{align*}

Likewise, since we're told that the remainder is $18$ when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+4),$ it follows from the remainder theorem that \begin{align*} 18 &= f(-4)\\ &= a(-4)^2 + b(-4) - 10\\ &= a(16) + b(-4) - 10\\ &= 16a - 4b - 10. \end{align*}

We now have the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} 0 = 4a - 2b - 10\\ 18 = 16a - 4b - 10. \end{cases} \]

Simplifying each equation, we get

\[ \begin{cases} 2a - b = 5 \\ 4a - b = 7. \end{cases} \]

To eliminate $a,$ we subtract the equations and get

\[ \begin{alignat}{2} 4&a-b &&= 7 \\ - \hspace{7pt} 2&a-b &&=5 \\ \hline 2&a &&=2. \end{alignat} \]

So, we get $2a=2,$ and hence $a=1.$ Finally, we substitute it into $2a - b = 5 $ to find $b=-3.$

Therefore, our final solution is $(a,b) = (1,-3).$

Finally then, $a+b=1-3=-2$
